requirement: Short links expire after a week. Redirect analytics are retained indefinitely. Expired links should still redirect for trusted partners.

stateTransitions.reason: material ambiguity detected; awaiting human clarification

s3RealResponse.affectedPath: Requirement 1a states a short link 'no longer resolves to a redirect' after expiry, implying expiry gates access to an unspecified underlying state, while requirement 1c requires the system to still resolve an expired short link to its target URL for trusted-partner requests. Whether 'expire' in 1a means the link mapping/target data is purged or merely that standard-path resolution is gated while the underlying record persists is never stated, and the two readings produce directly conflicting implementations: if expiry entails deletion or archival of the target-URL mapping, 1c becomes unsatisfiable for any link old enough to have been purged.
s3RealResponse.qualityChecksPerformed: Cross-referenced 1a's expiry behavior against 1c's trusted-partner exception to check whether both requirements can be satisfied by a single consistent data-lifecycle model; checked whether any of the three requirements defines what 'expire' does to underlying storage (deletion, soft-flag, archival) as opposed to just redirect behavior.

s3RealResponse.affectedPath: Requirement 1c's phrase 'requests identified as originating from a trusted partner' leaves both the definition of 'trusted partner' (an allowlisted account, an API key, an IP range, a contractual designation) and the identification mechanism/actor performing that classification (the redirect service itself, an upstream gateway, a header set by a reverse proxy) completely unspecified.
s3RealResponse.qualityChecksPerformed: Searched all three normalized requirements and this excerpt for any schema, enum, header name, or prior definition of 'trusted partner' or the identification signal; found none. Considered whether a standard framework default exists for partner/trust classification and found none applicable, since this is a domain-specific security-relevant concept, not a framework behavior.

s3RealResponse.affectedPath: Requirement 1a's '7 days after its creation timestamp' does not specify whether the 7-day window is measured as elapsed wall-clock time (168 hours from the exact creation instant) or as calendar days (e.g., expiring at a day boundary such as midnight UTC), nor does it specify the timezone/reference clock used for the comparison.
s3RealResponse.qualityChecksPerformed: Checked whether an existing approved artifact (schema, prior clarification, or timestamp-format convention) already fixes elapsed-time vs. calendar-day semantics for this feature; none found in the provided requirements. Considered whether this is a reasonable, uncontested framework default, but expiry boundary semantics are domain policy, not a framework behavior, so no uncontested default applies.

s3RealResponse.affectedPath: Requirement 1c requires continued redirect for trusted-partner requests to an expired short link but states no time bound on this exception — it is unclear whether the trusted-partner redirect capability holds indefinitely (matching 1b's indefinite analytics retention) or is itself capped at some retention horizon after which even trusted-partner requests would fail to resolve.
s3RealResponse.qualityChecksPerformed: Checked 1b for any retention bound that might implicitly apply to the underlying link/target-URL data (as opposed to analytics records) and found 1b speaks only to analytics records, not to the short link mapping itself, leaving the duration of the 1c exception unconstrained by any other requirement in this set.

s3RealResponse.affectedPath: Requirement 1b mandates that redirect analytics be retained indefinitely 'including analytics associated with expired short links,' but none of the three requirements states whether a trusted-partner redirect that occurs after a link's nominal expiry (per the 1c exception) itself generates a new analytics record, or whether 1b's guarantee covers only analytics captured prior to expiry.
s3RealResponse.qualityChecksPerformed: Checked whether 1b's retention guarantee, read together with 1c's redirect exception, implies an obligation to record post-expiry trusted-partner redirect events; found no acceptance criterion in any of the three requirements that commits to (or excludes) generating analytics for that specific event class.

s3RealResponse.affectedPath: Requirement 1b's phrase 'retained indefinitely and SHALL NOT be automatically deleted or expired' is unbounded in duration by design.
s3RealResponse.qualityChecksPerformed: Checked whether any stated obligation (functional requirement, gate condition, or scope boundary in this set) imposes a competing retention cap that 'indefinitely' would conflict with; found none.
s3RealResponse.noClarificationReason: The plain-language meaning of 'indefinitely' and 'SHALL NOT be automatically deleted or expired' is unambiguous and directly implementable as 'never delete via automated process' — every conformant implementation behaves identically (no automatic deletion path exists) regardless of how the term is further parsed, so there is no behavioural fork.

s3RealResponse.affectedPath: The terms 'short link' and 'redirect to its target URL' used across 1a and 1c are not formally defined in this excerpt.
s3RealResponse.qualityChecksPerformed: Checked whether 'short link' or 'target URL' admit multiple plausible domain interpretations that would change implementation behavior; both are standard, unambiguous URL-shortener domain vocabulary (a generated short path mapping to an original destination URL) used consistently across all three requirements with no competing usage.
s3RealResponse.noClarificationReason: The ordinary, plain-language meaning of these terms already suffices to implement correctly — the requirements author's own consistent usage across 1a/1b/1c fixes the meaning, and no conformant implementation could reasonably diverge on what a 'short link' or its 'target URL' are.

s2RealResponse.statement: A short link SHALL expire 7 days after its creation timestamp, after which it no longer resolves to a redirect for standard (non-trusted-partner) requests.
Redirect analytics records SHALL be retained indefinitely and SHALL NOT be automatically deleted or expired, including analytics associated with expired short links.
For requests identified as originating from a trusted partner, the system SHALL continue to redirect an expired short link to its target URL rather than treating it as expired.
